label: fed-back f input early in the copy phase, strongest when outputting f or r
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is f (a fed-back copied f). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase or on any other input. Activity sits early in the copy: recall_idx 1 holds 77% of mass and recall_idx 2 holds 20%, with nothing past recall_idx 4. Usually this is the step right after <DEL>, in sequences that start with f. It fires on only about 3% of copy-phase f inputs (precision 0.027 for in_tok==f). Among those, it is much more likely and stronger when the token being output is f or r (out_tok f/r carries 68% of mass; the top examples are f f i.. and f r i..). It is also stronger for short sequences (L 3-4) and when i follows. The f/r-output clause catches about half the active steps and two thirds of the mass. The remaining activations are weak and spread over many output tokens, so the exact selection among f inputs is not fully captured. The broader predicate in_tok==f & recall_idx<=2 in the copy phase covers 97% of mass but has precision 0.07.
